title: Evaluate asymmetric input/output unit pricing and minimum-billing variants for Hosted API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Sales and Legal continue to ask for clearer contract language and examples for per-unit billing; customers also report confusion about charges on streaming responses vs. buffer/batched tokens. Goal: Run a controlled set of pricing experiments to validate (1) asymmetric input vs. output unit pricing (IO split) as a lever to better reflect server-side cost and customer value, and (2) minimum-billing (per-request or per-minute floors) variants to reduce noise from many tiny streaming calls. These experiments should feed pricing guidance, contract language snippets for security questionnaires, and a recommended default for the Hosted API billing engine.
experiment_design: Primary hypothesis: Charging output tokens at a premium to input tokens (e.g., output:input = 1.3x) will increase revenue per-request while preserving adoption for generative use-cases where output is the primary cost driver.

Secondary hypothesis: Introducing a small per-response minimum (example: charge minimum equivalent to 5 output tokens for streaming requests under 5 tokens) reduces per-call billing variance without materially impacting developer satisfaction for normal traffic patterns.

Arms: A (control): current flat per-token rate; B (IO split - mild): input=1x, output=1.15x; C (IO split - strong): input=1x, output=1.35x; D (minimum floor): control rates but add per-response floor = 5 output tokens; E (combined): IO split mild + floor.
Sample pricing numbers for simulation: control=0.0003$/token; B output=0.000345$/token; C output=0.000405$/token; floor= min charge of 0.0015$/request.

Segmentation: run experiments across three customer cohorts: self-serve low-volume (free trial users), PLG-mid (frequent dev/test usage, < $2k/month), and enterprise (sales-contracted customers eligible for experiments only after legal opt-in).
Duration: 6 weeks per cohort with rolling traffic split (10% to each treatment for self-serve; 5% for PLG-mid to reduce impact).

Measurement windows: weekly revenue, churn signal (downgrade/stop), API call volume, average tokens per call (in/out), median latency, developer support tickets per 1000 calls, NPS change for trial users (optional survey).

Signups & Informed consent: experiments on self-serve cohort can be A/B tested with standard terms; sales-contracted enterprise customers require opt-in and updated pricing examples in the SOW/contract before exposure.
Data collection: use billing-raw (per-invoice line items), console telemetry (route-level token distribution), and customer support tags.
Success criteria: uplift in revenue per request >= 8% for PLG-mid without >3% increase in churn; no significant support ticket spike in self-serve arm (threshold: <15% relative increase).
success_metrics: Net new MRR movement in PLG-mid cohort
Support ticket rate (tickets per 10k API calls)
Average tokens billed per request (input vs output) change
Average latency: ensure no regression attributable to billing instrumentation (<5% change)
Legal & Sales acceptance: contract language drafted and signed off for enterprise FAQs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (preparation): finalize pricing arms, update billing simulator, create tracking dashboards, draft contract language snippets and security q&A examples. Target complete by 2026-02-18.
Phase 1 (self-serve): deploy A/B on self-serve sandbox and production with 10% traffic split. Monitor for 6 weeks. Provide opt-out in billing console for early testers.
Phase 2 (PLG-mid): deploy reduced-surface experiment (5% traffic per arm) after validating no major issues in Phase 1.
Phase 3 (enterprise pilot): run a small pilot with 3 enterprise customers with contractual opt-in; include explicit examples in their pricing schedules and security questionnaire responses.

Phase 4 (analysis & decision): combine telemetry + finance simulations and recommend either (a) adopt IO split mild across Hosted API with floor for streaming, (b) adopt floor only, or (c) retain flat pricing. Prepare release notes and contract language templates.
Rollback criteria: if any cohort shows >3x expected support tickets, >5% absolute churn increase, or material legal disputes, immediately pause the affected arm and revert billing on that cohort.

risks_mitigation: Risk: Developer backlash vs perceived hidden charging. Mitigation: clear UI estimates, billing previews, and email notices to test participants.
Risk: Contract disputes with enterprise. Mitigation: require written opt-in and include worked examples in SOW; Legal to pre-approve FAQ language.
Risk: Measurement noise from differing tokenization. Mitigation: normalize using our shared tokenizer preprocess; use median and trimmed means in analysis.

Risk: Implementation complexity in billing engine. Mitigation: build experiment flagging layer to compute delta charges without changing canonical billing path; small rollout to validate before hard changes.
